content:
alex_ryan: FYI getting a compliance alert — audit log shows multiple requests for EU tenant `acct_78` served from us-east-1 during a fallback window. :rotating_light:
maria_chen: copy. Which alert ID? can you paste the audit snippet?
alex_ryan: audit_id=AU-2026-09-12-9083, snippet below:
```
> timestamp=2026-09-12T14:02:11Z audit_event=RESIDENCY_BYPASS tenant=acct_78 route=chat.generate original_region=eu-west-1 served_region=us-east-1 fallback_reason=POOL_EXHAUSTED decision_version=3.2.1
```
chris_patel: looking at router logs now — I see a cluster of fallback decisions between 14:01 and 14:05. Reason is POOL_EXHAUSTED with policy weight that allowed cross-region fallback.
nina_garcia: customer reported higher latency at the same time, also they flagged that the request body included eu-data residency requirement. Ticket INC-4312 opened, assigning ops+compliance.
ops-bot: Automated alert: residency-violation-detected for tenant acct_78 (AUDIT: AU-2026-09-12-9083). Notifying #incidents and compliance.
alex_ryan: repro steps I ran locally (short):
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-User-Region: eu" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
2) check response headers -> x-served-region shows us-east-1 for some requests
Example header: `x-served-region: us-east-1`
maria_chen: can you paste the full router decision log for one of the affected request IDs? the one with decision_version=3.2.1.
alex_ryan: pasted below (sanitized):
```
request_id=rc_9a7f decision=FALLBACK selected_pool=dense-us fallback_policy="allow_cross_region:true, prefer_local:false, strict_residency:false" capacity_snapshot={eu:0, us:12}
```
chris_patel: aha — config shows prefer_local=false for that rollout. That rollout was part of a performance experiment last week (rollout id R-2026-08-31-perf). We unintentionally relaxed strict residency in the experiment config.
nina_garcia: can we confirm whether billing or tokens were double counted? customer claims unexpected cost spike.
alex_ryan: billing looks normal; tokens served were from us-east but metered same way. main issue is policy violation and audit noise.
compliance-bot: Policy exception logged: EXC-772. Recommended action: notify customer, patch routing policy, run retrospective audit for past 24h.
maria_chen: immediate mitigation: revert rollout R-2026-08-31-perf to previous config and set strict_residency=true for tenants with residency flags. I can push a config rollback now.
chris_patel: if we rollback, we might hit queueing in eu cluster. Suggest short-term throttle + burst allocation to eu for affected customers. I'll provision emergency burst (5 GPUs) for eu pool and update autoscaler limits.
nina_garcia: I'll draft a customer message: apologize, explain fallback due to capacity exhaustion during a perf experiment, note we've reverted config and will provide audit logs. Tagging compliance for wording.
alex_ryan: running rollback command now: `./ops/rollout rollback R-2026-08-31-perf --reason "residency-violation" --who maria_chen`
ops-bot: Rollout R-2026-08-31-perf rollback started by maria_chen at 2026-09-12T14:07:03Z. CI checks passed.
chris_patel: eu burst provision started, ETA ~3m. Also changing router policy default to `strict_residency=true` for managed-tenants until we finish audit.
compliance-bot: Noted. Creating compliance ticket COMP-988, collecting affected request IDs. Reminder: preserve logs for 90 days.
maria_chen: rollback complete. Confirming router now returns `x-served-region: eu-west-1` for my tests.
alex_ryan: re-running the original repro curl — now served_region=eu-west-1 consistently. Latency improved for the customer too.
nina_garcia: sending customer update now. Draft: "We detected cross-region failovers for a subset of requests during a recent performance rollout. We've reverted the rollout, provisioned additional EU capacity, and logged this as a compliance exception. We will share the audit bundle."
chris_patel: followups: 1) revert experiment config from git and add a guard to prevent strict_residency toggles in experiments; 2) run traffic replay for last 4h to identify all affected tenants; 3) add an alert that ties audit_event=RESIDENCY_BYPASS to rollout changes.
maria_chen: I'll create PRs and the alert rule. tagging @security for a quick review of the retrospective audit results.
alex_ryan: thanks all. mark as active incident until compliance closes COMP-988 and customer confirms. :white_check_mark:
